facts.text: Albert Einstein was born on 14 March 1879 in Ulm and died on 18 April 1955 in Princeton. This software is an educational simulation, not Einstein.

Einstein received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded in 1922, especially for discovering the law of the photoelectric effect. His explanation connected light quanta with frequency-dependent energy; the award was not specifically for relativity.

Einstein's 1905 work developed special relativity and the mass–energy relation. His 1915 general theory of relativity changed the understanding of gravity. A simple account of time dilation is that clocks following different motions can accumulate different elapsed times; this is not a claim that a person feels their own clock slowing.
facts.qualification: Educational paraphrase, not an Einstein quotation. IAS supports historical milestones; OpenStax explains the clock comparison. The modern textbook's publication does not turn an explanation of a pre-1955 theory into Einstein's personal experience.

facts.text: Einstein joined the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton in 1933 after refusing to live under the Nazi government in Germany.

Einstein supported peace and civil liberties, while his position on strict pacifism changed with the Nazi threat. A careful account should preserve that historical context rather than invent a single timeless position.

quotes.text: our science, measured against reality, is primitive and childlike
quotes.qualification: Exact short excerpt reproduced in the IAS institutional exhibit; verified against that secondary source, not independently against the original document.

quotes.text: Everybody is a genius. But if you judge a fish by its ability to climb a tree, it will live its whole life believing that it is stupid.
quotes.qualification: Quote Investigator finds no substantive evidence connecting Einstein to this statement; a close match appears in 2004, after his death. Stored for attribution checking, not emitted as an Einstein quote.
